label: GO WITH CONDITIONS
call: Run a 90-day pilot of one channel under 'science and history, told as stories,' with 'what if' as the labelled lead. Four long videos cut into native pieces, each linking a paid Odoo offer, at 4 founder hours a week with Odoo work scheduled first. Do not commit to a niche yet. Stop on day 60 or day 90 if the Odoo signals do not come.

why.point: Views do not pay. The test is a signed Odoo client, not views. Four thousand watch hours earns about $200 to $400 a year at vendor RPMs.
The hours are the real price. Each long video displaces about $300 of client work, so the cap is 4 hours a week and Odoo is scheduled first.
One channel with a labelled format umbrella keeps one audience alive when a topic fails. Tag every piece by format and read results by format at day 60.

minority.quote: Five long videos is not a test, and I said so in Round 2 (volume before verdict, S052). Set the test unit at ten or more offer-linked pieces, and make day 90 continue only at one-to-one on hours: five signed Odoo clients.
minority.would_have_to_be_true: One signed client does not pay for the hours. The first 90 days would have to yield five signed clients at $320 gross profit each to break even on about $1,560 of forgone work.

next_steps.action: Write the kill criteria in a dated file, write the Odoo billing rate at the top of the hour log, and start the two-week hour log.
Name the 100 people who would be upset if the channel stopped (fewer than 30 stops it), and check the first video's hours against the 10-hour estimate.

Read views, retention and traced Odoo inquiries by format. Stop on median under 300 views or average view under 35% duration, or on no traced inquiry. Switch the lead to history if fewer than two videos reached 1,000 views.

kill_criteria: Day 90: no signed Odoo client sourced from the channel, or Odoo billing down more than 10% from baseline. Either one ends the channel.
conditions: Kill criteria in a dated file before the first upload
Odoo billing rate written down; under $30 an hour raise the client price first; over $50 drop to one video a month
100 named people by day 14; fewer than 30 stops the channel
Two-week hour log; first video over 10 hours drops the pilot to two long videos
Channel hours capped at 4 a week, cuts included; more than 4 for three straight weeks pauses the channel
Every claim has a named primary source and a second check; failed episodes are pulled
Odoo billing within 10% of the three-month baseline; down more than 10% at day 45 pauses, at day 90 stops
Day 180 continue bar: five signed clients, at least the first on a fixed-price product
$150 cash cap over 90 days; tool spend under $50 a month

fights.story: Bezos and Martell wanted space and science what-if; Buffett and Hormozi wanted untold history; Gary V and Graham wanted one umbrella with what-if as the labelled lead. Graham's argument won: a single niche can fail on its topic and lose the audience. Gary V moved to the umbrella shape. Bezos kept what-if as the lead and accepted a switch to history at day 60 if the views do not come. Format is tagged and read at day 60.

fights.crux: Does the channel earn anything beyond attention?
fights.story: Gary V and Bezos said attention is worth a cheap test. Hormozi, Buffett and Naval said views earn about $12 to $22 a month. All seven now agree only a paid Odoo offer counts as a result.

fights.crux: How many founder hours a week?
fights.story: Martell and Gary V wanted 3; Bezos, Buffett, Hormozi and Naval wanted 4. The Chair set 4 with cuts counted inside the cap. Four videos, not five, because five at 10 hours leaves no slack for the cuts.

amendments.amendment: Odoo billing down more than 10% at day 90 is an automatic stop.
amendments.reason: No seat objected; Buffett already had it.

amendments.amendment: Day 60 stop on median under 300 views or average view under 35% duration, regardless of inquiries.
amendments.reason: The draft joined the two with AND, which let a channel failing on viewers survive on one inquiry.

amendments.amendment: Test unit of ten or more offer-linked pieces.
amendments.reason: Adopted in part: the unit is pieces cut from four long videos, each linking an offer, which covers the ten.

amendments.amendment: Day 90 continues only at five signed clients.
amendments.reason: Day 90 is a read. One signed client is the day-90 bar, and five is the day-180 bar. Recorded in the minority report.

amendments.amendment: Continue rule requires a fixed-price Odoo product, not a custom project.
amendments.reason: Applied to the day-180 bar. Day 90 stays one signed client of any kind; the objection is recorded in the minority report.

amendments.amendment: Six native cuts per long video are the test unit, logged against the hour cap.
amendments.reason: Covers the test unit and keeps the cuts inside the 4-hour cap.

amendments.amendment: Cap channel time at 3 hours a week, not 4.
amendments.reason: Four seats set 4. Recorded in the minority report.

amendments.amendment: Cap at 3 hours and four videos.
amendments.reason: The 3-hour cap is not adopted (see Gary V). Four videos is adopted.

amendments.amendment: Day-60 gate: no paid Odoo inquiry traced to the channel means stop.
amendments.reason: Early Odoo signal is the only income test under $1,000 a month revenue.

amendments.amendment: Day-90 bar is one signed Odoo client, not an inquiry.
amendments.reason: An inquiry costs nothing to count and pays nothing.

cheapest_test: The two-week hour log, then one long video with a paid Odoo link. Under $150 and about 20 founder hours.
revisit: Day 60, with views, retention and traced inquiries by format; day 90, with signed Odoo clients and billing.
